name: Publishing production of a title
one_line: The PUBLISHER-side record of one title becoming a product: a delivered manuscript transmitted into production, typeset into pass pages, jacketed against a printer-confirmed spine width, given a permanent product identifier and a price, described in a machine-readable record that a retailer and a library ingest, scheduled onto a season alongside OTHER TITLES, and manufactured against a print specification. Its distinguishing structure is that the same text exists simultaneously as three different objects with three different identity systems - a document with a version family, a layout with linked assets and licensed fonts, and a PRODUCT with an identifier - and only the third has no home anywhere else in the tree. It is not the author's own manuscript folder (creative.book-manuscript), not the packet an author sends an agent (creative.submission-query), not a printed artefact whose job stops at the printer (creative.print-production), and not a recurring dated issue (creative.periodical-issue). Placeholder template on the field-less creative schema: it writes NO field rows and therefore recommends NO folder dimensions.

deterministic: PRECONDITION, inherited verbatim in force from the creative schema: every entry below is a DETECTION signal and never an extraction licence. This template's schema declares no field rows, so nothing here writes a domain fact. Detection exists so the material is recognised as a title in production, kept local while the on-sale date has not passed, and offered as one production set rather than scattered by format. "Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector."

A DISTRIBUTION-METADATA RECORD: a structured product feed or its export - an ONIX-shaped XML document, or a spreadsheet whose column headers are product-supply-chain headers (product identifier, format, binding, extent, trim, price by currency, publication date, imprint, subject code, contributor role). 00 requires the extractor to yield exactly the parts that make this legible: "Source code, notebooks, configuration files, and structured data formats such as Python, JavaScript, SQL, Jupyter notebooks, JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, and CSV should yield readable text plus format-specific structure such as language, imports, notebook cell types, package manifests, schema keys, repository markers, and project-root signals" and "Spreadsheets such as XLSX, XLS, CSV, TSV, ODS, and Numbers exports should yield workbook or file metadata, sheet names, column headers, visible cell values, table-like regions, formulas only when useful, and dates or identifiers from labeled cells". THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST ROW-SPECIFIC STRUCTURE IN THE FAMILY. No other creative sibling emits a machine-readable product record addressed to a third-party supply chain; a poster, a brand identity, a film cut and a music session have deliverables but no product identity.

A MULTI-TITLE SCHEDULE: a spreadsheet or table whose ROWS are distinct works and whose COLUMNS are production milestones - manuscript due, transmittal, first pass, jacket approval, files to printer, printer delivery, on-sale. The multiplicity is the signal and it is what separates this row from every author-side row, which by construction sees one work. A one-row schedule is not this signal.

A PRINT SPECIFICATION coupled to a JACKET: a specification document carrying paper stock, bulk, extent, trim size, binding style and run length, PLUS a cover or jacket working file whose stem or interior geometry carries a spine measurement. The COUPLING is the signal, and it is a real production dependency rather than a described one - the jacket cannot be drawn until the printer confirms bulk, so a spine value appearing in a filename is derived evidence that a manufacturing spec exists.

A TRANSMITTAL or HANDOVER document: a short form naming a work, an author, an editor, a word or page extent, a delivered state and a receiving production department. It is 00's purpose-coherence shape for this world - a document that says what a set of files is FOR rather than what it is about - and it is what makes an editorially incoherent folder one title.

A PASS-PAGES SEQUENCE: a run of proof PDFs across ordinal rounds (first pass, second pass, revises) carrying typeset page numbers, running heads and folio structure, each accompanied or followed by a marked-up return. 00 collects the structural half universally - "duplicate and version-family signals" - and here the family is a production round rather than an author's revision.

A TITLE-LEVEL FINANCIAL MODEL: a spreadsheet whose labelled rows are print run, unit manufacturing cost, list price, discount, royalty rate, advance earn-out and contribution. This is the artefact of the publishing DECISION and it exists on the publisher's side only; an author never builds one.

AN IDENTIFIER-NAMED ASSET SET: retail-facing files whose stems are the product identifier rather than the title - a cover image sized for a retailer, an interior sample, a metadata sidecar. An identifier-shaped stem alone is a bare number and is listed in never_alone; the signal is an identifier stem RESOLVING to a title that is independently evidenced in the same corpus.

A PERMISSIONS or CLEARANCE LOG: a table of quoted or reproduced third-party material with rightsholder, extent, territory, fee and clearance state. It belongs to production rather than to writing, because it is generated when a delivered manuscript is audited for what it borrows.
needs_llm: Deciding whether a folder holding one novel's proofs, jacket and print spec is a publisher's production set or an author's archive of what the publisher sent them. The bytes are identical and the discriminator is the presence of production-side apparatus that an author never generates - a schedule with other titles on it, a P&L, a printer purchase order, a distribution feed. Where none is present, prefer creative.book-manuscript or abstain.

Separating a title production set from a print job that merely happens to be a book-shaped object - a self-published print run, a conference proceedings, a commemorative volume. The reading turns on whether a PRODUCT identity and a distribution record exist, not on whether the object has pages and a spine.
Reading catalogue and sales-sheet copy, which is marketing prose about a work and is easily mistaken for the work itself, or for reading material the corpus owner saved.

Interpreting an ordinal round word ('first pass', 'second revises', 'blues', 'F&Gs') in context, because the same words appear in creative.print-production and in creative.revision-round with different meanings.

Judging whether a foreign-language edition file belongs to this title's production set or to a separately held translation engagement, which is a real seam against creative.translation-project rather than a formatting question.
never_alone: A PUBLISHER'S OR IMPRINT'S NAME. This is the never-alone case that would sink the row if it were allowed: an imprint name appears on the copyright page of every book anyone has ever downloaded, on a reader's ebook, on a review copy, on a catalogue a bookseller saved. 00's own prohibition on an organisation name as sole proof governs. An imprint name may retrieve a candidate for local review; it may never activate this row.

A BARE PRODUCT-IDENTIFIER-SHAPED NUMBER. A 13-digit stem is a bare number and 00 forbids a bare number as sole proof. `9780000000001.pdf` sitting alone is an unidentified PDF, not a title in production. The identifier must resolve to a title independently evidenced in the same corpus.

THE WORD 'manuscript', 'proof', 'galley', 'ARC', 'jacket' or 'pages' IN A FILENAME. Every one of these is a work_type value already declared by the creative schema, and a filename token is exactly the observation-not-fact case. `2nd pass pages.pdf` with no title, no schedule and no spec is a Review Later file.

A BOOK-SHAPED PDF WITH FRONT MATTER. A title page, copyright page, contents and running heads describe a book that exists, not a book being made. A purchased ebook, a downloaded public-domain scan and a self-published volume all carry them. Reading Inbox is the honest home.
AN .indd OR .idml EXTENSION. The extension is a routing signal; 00 treats it as such and not as an assumption about meaning. A layout file is equally a menu, a report, a zine or an annual review.

THE ABSENCE OF AN AUTHOR'S WORKING FILES. This row must not be activated on a negative - 'no .docx drafts present, therefore publisher-side' is not evidence. A corpus can lack drafts because they were deleted, because the author works elsewhere, or because a single delivered file is all there ever was.

A ROUND WORD PLUS A DATE. `Nightwork 2026-04-12 R2.pdf` carries a version-family signal that 00 already collects universally for every file in the corpus. It supports a group; it does not choose this row over creative.revision-round or creative.book-manuscript.

grouping_reasons: one title across its transmitted manuscript, typeset layout, proof rounds, jacket, print files and product record
one production round - what pass pages went out on a date and what corrections came back
one season or list, recognised by a multi-title schedule whose rows are distinct works
one print job at one printer, recognised by a specification, a purchase order and a matching files-to-printer package
one product identifier and every asset named for it, where the identifier independently resolves to an evidenced title
one contract and the rights, permissions and royalty material that references the same named work
an existing curated folder the publishing team already made and named for a title

template.why: EMPTY BY CONTRACT, NOT BY JUDGEMENT, AND THE SECOND LIMB OF THE NODE TEST IS THEREFORE CONCEDED RATHER THAN CLAIMED. A dimension may only branch on a field the schema declares, and the creative schema declares none, so this row cannot differ from the default on dimensions and does not pretend to. Held as prose for the pass that may declare fields: this row's order is the schema default UNCHANGED - project (the title), then stage (the production milestone), then artifact_type - with the client level omitted, because in publishing the counterparty relation INVERTS. The maker is the publisher and the author is the supplier, so `client` would either be empty or would wrongly name the author as the commissioner. The parent-context test fixes the rest - "a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child" - and `2nd pass pages` is meaningless without the title exactly as Homework 3 is meaningless without the course. NOT TIME-FIRST: "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." This row does NOT hold either of the two time-first exceptions the schema names by title; a season or list is a scheduling fact and not capture-based media, and claiming time-first from a pub-date column would be claiming the photos exception without the photos evidence. ONE PROHIBITION this row would add if fields ever land: no per-proof-round folder level below artifact_type, because rounds are a version family and 00 already collects "duplicate and version-family signals" universally without needing a branch. Whatever lands stays advisory: "The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions."

collides_with.signal: THE LOAD-BEARING COLLISION OF THIS ROW, and the reciprocal is already authored on the neighbour, which names the same fixture. SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `Nightwork - 1st pass pages.pdf`. BOOK-MANUSCRIPT claims it as proofs arriving into one work's folder beside that work's own manuscript version family - the AUTHOR-SIDE holding. THIS ROW claims it as one member of a production set that also contains a multi-title schedule, a print specification, a distribution metadata record and a title P&L - the PUBLISHER-SIDE holding. RECIPROCAL, stated in both directions: the presence of production-side apparatus is this row's decisive evidence and its absence is book-manuscript's; neither side may claim the other's from the proof pages alone. THIS ROW ADDITIONALLY CONCEDES that it must never claim an author's numbered draft run (`Nightwork - Draft 7.docx`), which is book-manuscript's alone, and must never activate from an imprint name on a copyright page. The neighbour's NJ-BM-4 records the unresolved half - whether a corpus-shape observation may inform a file-level activation - and this row carries the same open question rather than pretending to have settled it.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `Nightwork - Print Spec and Quote - Ravenscroft Press.pdf` and the jacket working file beside it. PRINT-PRODUCTION claims any print job by its manufacturing apparatus - specification, quotation, proof round, imposition, press approval - and its unit is the JOB. THIS ROW claims the same documents only when the job is manufacturing one member of a titled, identifier-bearing, scheduled list whose text arrived as a manuscript. RECIPROCAL: print-production must not claim a title's whole production set merely because a printer document sits in it, and THIS ROW MUST NOT CLAIM A PRINT JOB WITH NO TITLE AND NO PRODUCT RECORD - the poster fixture is precisely that case and it is print-production's. Where a book is printed with no distribution record and no list, print-production is the correct reading and this row abstains: "Correct abstention is a successful outcome because the product’s goal is reliable organization, not maximum file movement."

SAME STRUCTURE, DIFFERENT UNIT, and the confusable evidence is the whole production apparatus - transmittal, layout, pass pages, print spec, files to printer. PERIODICAL-ISSUE's unit is a DATED ISSUE ON A RECURRING CADENCE with an issue number, a flatplan and a repeating masthead, and its schedule rows are issues of one publication. THIS ROW's unit is a TITLE WITH A PERMANENT PRODUCT IDENTIFIER that appears once, and its schedule rows are distinct works. RECIPROCAL: a periodical must not be claimed here because it has a print spec and an identifier (periodicals carry serial identifiers too), and this row must not be claimed by periodical-issue because a season schedule looks like a publication calendar. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS WHETHER THE ROWS ARE WORKS OR DATES. Annuals and part-works sit genuinely on this line and neither row should force them.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: a full delivered manuscript file. SUBMISSION-QUERY claims it as a member of a purpose-coherent packet addressed OUTWARD by an author - a query letter, a synopsis, an agency tracking list. THIS ROW claims it as material transmitted INWARD into production - a transmittal form, a receiving department, a schedule slot. RECIPROCAL: this row must never absorb a query letter, a synopsis or a submissions tracker, none of which are production; and submission-query must not claim a transmittal form because it is a short covering document naming a work. The discriminator is the DIRECTION of the addressee, not the content.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: a foreign-language edition of the same named work, and a rights grid cell naming a licensee. TRANSLATION-PROJECT claims the translator-side engagement - a source text beside a target text, a glossary or style sheet, a segmented working file, a commissioning counterparty. THIS ROW claims the licensor-side register - a territory grid, a licence, an advance against a foreign edition. RECIPROCAL: a translation engagement is not a publishing production set because the work is the same title, and this row must not claim a translator's working files because it holds the rights grid that led to them.

Inherited from the schema's load-bearing collision and true of this row's own material. A jacket, a designed interior spread or a finished title PDF is simultaneously a deliverable of a production and the third page of a designer's or editor's portfolio. The discriminator is what the file is FOR: production apparatus around it (spec, schedule, proofs, transmittal) is this row; a curated set of finished exports ordered for showing, beside a resume or a reel, is career. RECIPROCAL: career must not claim a live jacket working file because it is the designer's best work, and this row must not claim a portfolio export because it depicts a book.

also_holds_with.signal: The author agreement, the permissions clearances and the subsidiary-rights licences are legally operative instruments AND the rights record of a specific title. The evidence is disjoint - numbered clauses, defined terms, a parties block and an execution block on one side; the named work, its territory, its formats and its royalty schedule on the other. "One file may hold facts from more than one domain without losing information." Neither reading may suppress the other, and where an instrument carries an individual's identifying or financial details the protective posture governs handling regardless of which reading is more informative for placement.

The title P&L, the printer purchase order, the royalty statement and the print quotation are production artefacts AND independent financial evidence. Disjoint evidence: a title, a run length and a production milestone on one side; an issuer, a period, an amount and a payment state on the other. Filed as coactivation rather than collision because the two do not compete for the same evidence item - a royalty statement genuinely is both the record of a title's performance and a financial document.

An in-house publishing team's material carries both readings: a season launch is a production programme AND a marketing programme with a budget, an approval chain and a reporting line. Disjoint evidence - transmittals, proofs and print files on one side; a controlled-document header, an approval block and a period-and-variance table on the other. A catalogue PDF is genuinely both a designed artefact of this row and a governing sales document of the business.

Also listed as a collision, and both edges are true of different files. The legitimate double reading: the jacket working file and the files-to-printer package ARE a print job and ARE a title's production - the same bytes, two honest readings on disjoint evidence (linked assets and spine geometry for the layout; stock, bulk and run length for the job). What must not happen is the double reading being used to pull a poster or a packaging job into a title's set, or a whole title's editorial material into a print job.

falls_through_to.why: THE PRINCIPAL FALLTHROUGH FOR THIS ROW, and the honest one, because the normal case here is a real-looking production file whose SIDE is unresolved - a proof, a round word, a typeset PDF that could be author-held or publisher-held. "Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision."

The home for the row's commonest false positive: a finished book, a catalogue, a sample chapter or an advance information sheet that the corpus owner simply acquired. "Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association."

A standalone transmittal, a lone signed permission or a single delivered title PDF with a durable purpose and no production set around it. "Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group."

Author agreements with advance and royalty terms, royalty statements naming an individual's earnings, and embargoed proofs need the protective home rather than the informative one. "Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts."

Ordinary rather than exceptional here: password-protected production archives, proprietary layout packages and print-ready containers no approved extractor reads. "Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats."

The transactional edge of a production - a printer invoice, a permissions fee receipt, a proofreading contractor payment - where no title register is active to hold it. "Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents."

Retailer listing grabs, metadata-portal captures and reviewed-comment screenshots are a working habit of this world and most are disposable. "Temporary Screenshots may live under Photos/Temporary Screenshots and hold screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship."

sensitivity_why: Inherits the creative schema's unpublished-work posture, and claims ONE difference that is genuinely this row's - marked INFERENCE, and argued rather than asserted, because the third limb of the node test is the only limb besides detection that is available to a field-less template. THE CONFIDENTIALITY HERE IS SCHEDULED, NOT PERMANENT, AND THE SCHEDULE IS PRINTED INSIDE THE FILE. A proof, a jacket, catalogue copy and an advance reading copy are secret until an on-sale date and public after it, and the file itself frequently states the boundary ('uncorrected proof - not for quotation', an embargo line naming a date). Every other creative row's secrecy is open-ended - a campaign is confidential until launch with no date in the artefact, a source is confidential forever. The concrete consequence is a trap rather than a slogan: a DATE INSIDE A FILE MUST NOT BE READ AS AN EXPIRY. A past on-sale date does not make a locally held proof public, because the proof is not the published text, and an embargo the corpus owner cannot verify has lifted must be treated as live. Against that: "Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector." TWO FURTHER REASONS, both real and neither novel. (1) THIRD-PARTY FINANCIAL TERMS. An author agreement and a royalty statement carry an individual's advance, rate, earnings and balance - a person who is not the corpus owner and who never gave those figures to a filing agent. This is closer to Finance's posture than to Creative's, and it is why Protected Records rather than Review Later is the fallthrough for those two fixtures specifically. (2) A PSEUDONYM IS A LINK, not a name. Where a title is published under one name and its contract, royalty and permissions material carries another, the sensitive content is the CORRESPONDENCE between them, and a filesystem that co-locates the two discloses it by structure alone with no content ever being read. This row does NOT carry is_safety_domain - that flag stays with 00's four - and it assigns no handling class, which is P7's vocabulary.
open_question: Four, and the first is inherited from a neighbour that raised it against this row by name. (1) NJ-PT-1, THE CORPUS-SHAPE PROBLEM - THE SAME QUESTION AS NJ-BM-4, RESTATED FROM THIS SIDE. This row's decisive evidence against creative.book-manuscript is the presence of OTHER TITLES, which is an observation about the corpus rather than about a file, while activation reasons about files. If a corpus-shape observation is inadmissible at activation, this row loses its cleanest discriminator. The alternatives: (a) permit corpus-shape observations to inform activation, which is a change to the activation algorithm and affects far more than this row; (b) redraw the seam per-file on the presence of a production-side artefact type that an author never generates - a title P&L, a printer purchase order, a distribution metadata record - which is weaker but local, and is the fallback this row would take; (c) merge the two rows and let a role facet distinguish them, which cannot be done while the schema declares no field to hold the role. THIS ROW RECOMMENDS (b) AND DOES NOT TAKE IT, because taking it unilaterally would silently contradict the neighbour's authored reciprocal. R1c must settle both rows in one decision. (2) NJ-PT-2, THE PRODUCT IDENTIFIER IS A REAL FIELD-SHAPED HOLE AND NO KEY IS MINTED. A published title has a permanent product identifier that is neither a title nor a project name, that resolves assets to works, that is the join key of every distribution record in this world, and that no canonical key holds. It is deliberately not proposed: minting a key on a field-less schema is the 574's mistake at the point of maximum temptation, and the neighbour declined the identical temptation for a book's own identifier. The alternatives if R1c disagrees: (a) leave it unrepresented; (b) let it ride as a searchable observation with no field, which is what this row assumes; (c) mint one identifier key shared with the schema's existing rights-and-licence hole, since a usage grant and a product identity are both product-level rather than document-level facts. This row recommends (b). (3) NJ-PT-3, THE COUNTERPARTY RELATION INVERTS AND THE DEFAULT TEMPLATE ASSUMES IT DOES NOT. The schema default's optional top level is `client`, meaning the commissioning organisation. In publishing the maker IS the organisation and the author is the SUPPLIER, so `client` is either empty or wrongly filled with the author's name - which would additionally make an individual's name a folder level, the exact authorship-as-destination case 00 forbids. If option (b) of NJ-R1a-1 lands, R1c must decide whether `client` is simply omitted for this row (this row's position), or whether the inversion needs its own representation, which would be a second role_split this row cannot author. (4) NJ-PT-4, WHERE DOES A SELF-PUBLISHED TITLE GO. A self-publishing author generates a genuine product record, a print spec and a distribution feed while holding all the author-side drafts too, so the seam that separates this row from creative.book-manuscript dissolves in exactly the case that is now most common. The alternatives: (a) both rows activate, which is honest and is what coactivation is for, but the schema exposes no field to record which reading is which; (b) this row wins whenever a distribution record exists, which would pull an author's whole draft history into a production set; (c) neither wins and the material routes to Review Later, which is safe and unhelpful. This row takes (a) as its working assumption and flags that it is untested against a real filesystem.
